neighbours.label: A general rule or procedure stated as instruction: a formula, a how-to recipe ('to find X, multiply ... by ...') or a grammar rule ('nouns ending in y form the plural by ...'), as opposed to narrative about the same things
fire: To convert Celsius to Fahrenheit, multiply by nine, divide by five and add thirty-two.
Verbs ending in a single consonant double it before adding “ing” (e.g., run, running).
To find the volume of a cylinder, multiply the area of the base by the height.
The standard form of a linear equation is y = mx + b, where m is the slope.
To check whether a number is divisible by three, add its digits and see if the sum is divisible by three.
Adjectives of one syllable form the comparative by adding “er” (e.g., tall, taller).
The perimeter of a rectangle is twice the length plus twice the width.
To measure your resting pulse, count the beats for fifteen seconds and multiply by four.
quiet: It was thirty-two degrees in the shade when we finally reached the village.
He was running late again, so he skipped breakfast and caught the bus.
The old water tank was a rusty cylinder about two metres high.
She drew a straight line across the page and labelled it with a date.
The three of us split the bill and left before the band started.
The taller of the two brothers worked at the harbour for years.
The rectangle of light from the window moved slowly across the floor.
His pulse was still racing when the doctor finally came in.

predictions: Formulas, how-to procedures and grammar rules reach 0.4-1.0 somewhere inside the rule (the operand, the quoted ending, the variable). Narrative or descriptive sentences on the same topics stay under 0.1.
